# Exercises for test-first.
#
# The verifier runs after the agent stops, so it cannot see the order of events. It checks
# what the order produces: tests whose expected values came from the specification and
# not from the code. Each one swaps the agent's implementation for plausible wrong ones
# and requires the agent's own tests to fail on every one of them. Tests written after
# the code, from what it returns, pass on the code and on its near misses alike.

# Spec with a boundary, a tie in the rounding and a rejected input.
[boundary-spec] implement price_after_discount in discount.py as README.md describes, with unittest tests in test_discount.py | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# Many rejections in the spec; each is one more way for tests derived from the code to stay silent.
[duration-validation] implement parse_duration in duration.py as README.md describes, with unittest tests in test_duration.py | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# A reported bug: the first step is a test that fails on the bug as it stands.
[bug-first] a customer says balance_after in interest.py gives too little for terms that are not whole years, such as 18 months, fix it | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# A reported bug whose obvious test (the plan table, the plan setter) passes on the broken code; only a test through the gateway, in both directions and with the window count, fails on it.
[plan-change] customers say that changing plan has no effect on how many requests they get, for example a free user who upgrades is still stopped at 5; README.md says the new limit applies on the next request in either direction, fix it without changing the Gateway or Accounts constructors and methods, and add unittest tests to the test files in this directory | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# quote.py disagrees with README.md on several rules at once; NOTES.txt is stale and the code follows it. The tests must be written from the README and kill every rule mutant
[shipping-quote] The order pricing in quote.py has been reported wrong for some orders. README.md is the specification. Before changing quote.py, write tests in a new file named test_quote_rules.py that state what README.md requires with values worked out by hand, run them and read the failures, then fix quote.py so they pass. Leave the existing tests in test_quote.py as they are. NOTES.txt is old. | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# contacts.py follows a stale docstring (7 digit phones, no email normalising, first match only); README.md is the spec. Needs tests for each key rule, transitivity in any order, and the tie and ordering rules
[contact-dedupe] Duplicate contacts are not being merged correctly. README.md is the specification. Before changing contacts.py, write tests in a new file named test_contact_rules.py that state what README.md requires with values worked out by hand, run them and read the failures, then fix contacts.py so they pass. Leave test_contacts.py as it is. The docstring in contacts.py is old. | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"
